main_text.p: תִּבְעֵרָה[?] f. Exarsio, Combustio; sed est ut Nomen proprium loci, Num.11.3.

בָּעַת Pih. Perterruit, Perturbavit: Præter. נִבְעֲתָהוּ Perturbant eum, Job.18.11. Partic. fœm. מְבַעַתְךָ Perturbat te, 1.Sam.16.15. Niph. Præter. נִבְעַת Territus fuit, Esth.7.6. נִבְעַתִּי Conturbatus fui, Dan.8.17.
בְּעוֹתִים m.p. Terrores, Conturbationes: Constr. בְּעוֹתֵי Job.6.4. Aff. בְּעוֹתֶיךָ Conturbationes tuæ, Psal.88.17.
בָּצָל m. Cepa: Plur. וְהַבְּצָלִים Et ceparum, scil. recordamur, Num.11.5.

בָּצַע Quæstum fecit, Quæstui vel avaritiæ dedītus fuit: Item Divisit, Discidit, Concidit; Concisus, Sauciatus fuit, Concidit se, & ita cum פָּצַע convenit, ב & פ inter se commutatis: Partic. בֹּצֵעַ בָּצַע רַע Quæstuosus quæstus mali, id est, Quæstui deditus, q.d. Quæstuans quæstum, Abac.2.9. Impér. [illegible, ~2 letters] וּבְצַע Et divide eos, Amos 9.1. cum duplici Pathach præter normam. Futur. יִבְצַע Concident se, Sauciabuntur, Joel.2.8. Pih. בִּצַּע Quæstum exercuit vel fecit, ut Ezech.22.12. Item Præcidit, Concidit, Resecuit, Jesa.38.12. Perfecit, Complevit, Jesa.10.12. Zach.4.9.
בְּצַע Frustulum, Segmentum, Judic.5. v.19. Quæstus, Lucrum, & in malum fere semper sumitur, Exod. 18. v.21.
בֵּץ m. Cœnum, Lutum: הַטִּבְעוּ בַּבֵּץ Demersi sunt in cœnum, Jer.38.22.
בְּצָרָה f. Idem, Job.8.11. Plurale cum א loco, ו, בְּצִאתָו Canosa[?] ejus, Ezech.47.11.
בָּצַק Incumuit: Præt. בָּצְקוּ Intumuerunt, Neh.9.21. בָּצְקָה Intumuit; Inflatus est, Deut.8.4.

page.notes: Printed "F 2" at foot is the gathering signature. Running head is Hebrew, as printed. Marked doubtful: the first Hebrew form in the "Imper." entry, which has an unclear leading sign; the Hebrew headword vowels and dagesh in several entries are approximate; "Canosa" is uncertain in the long-s print. The Hebrew forms in the entries were read from a small, blurred scan and may need checking against the original.
